questions.question_hindi:
बाल अधिकारों से संबंधित भारत के संविधान के निम्नलिखित प्रावधानों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. अनुच्छेद 21A: 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार।
II. अनुच्छेद 24: कारखानों आदि में बच्चों के नियोजन का प्रतिषेध।
III. अनुच्छेद 39(e): यह सुनिश्चित करना कि बच्चों की सुकुमार अवस्था (tender age) का दुरुपयोग न हो।
IV. अनुच्छेद 45: छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों के लिए प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखरेख और शिक्षा (ECCE) का प्रावधान।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-से कथन भारतीय संविधान के तहत बाल अधिकारों का सही निरूपण करते हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल I, II और IV
केवल II, III और IV
I, II, III और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the following constitutional provisions in India relating to child rights:
I. Article 21A: Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
II. Article 24: Prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous occupations.
III. Article 39(e): Directive Principle enjoining the State to ensure that the tender age of children is not abused.
IV. Article 45: Directive Principle providing for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years.
Which of the statements given above correctly represent child rights under the Indian Constitution?
options_english: I and II only
I, II and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
All four statements correctly reflect constitutional provisions safeguarding the rights and welfare of children in India:

1. Statement I is correct (Article 21A): Inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, Article 21A makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for all children aged 6 to 14 years, operationalized via the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.
2. Statement II is correct (Article 24): A fundamental right under Part III prohibiting the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment.
3. Statement III is correct (Article 39(e)): A Directive Principle of State Policy in Part IV directing the State to secure that the health and strength of workers and the 'tender age of children are not abused' and that citizens are not forced by economic necessity into avocations unsuited to their age or strength.
4. Statement IV is correct (Article 45): Amending Article 45 concurrently with the insertion of Article 21A via the 86th Amendment, 2002, this Directive Principle mandates that the State shall endeavor to provide early childhood care and education (ECCE) for all children until they complete the age of six years.

In addition, Article 39(f) mandates healthy development opportunities for children in freedom and dignity, and Article 51A(k) makes providing educational opportunities a Fundamental Duty of parents/guardians.

Therefore, all four provisions correctly represent constitutional child rights protections. Option (D) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
चारों कथन भारतीय संविधान में बाल अधिकारों और उनके संरक्षण के प्रमुख प्रावधानों का पूर्णतः सही निरूपण करते हैं:

1. कथन I सही है (अनुच्छेद 21A): 86वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 द्वारा संविधान में अंतःस्थापित किया गया। यह 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के सभी बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाता है। इसे लागू करने के लिए 'शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009' (RTE Act) बनाया गया।
2. कथन II सही है (अनुच्छेद 24): भाग III में मौलिक अधिकार जो स्पष्ट रूप से 14 वर्ष से कम आयु के किसी भी बच्चे को कारखानों, खानों या अन्य परिसंकटमय रोजगारों में नियोजित करने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लगाता है।
3. कथन III सही है (अनुच्छेद 39(e)): राज्य नीति का निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) जो राज्य को यह सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश देता है कि श्रमिकों के स्वास्थ्य तथा बालकों की 'सुकुमार अवस्था' (tender age) का दुरुपयोग न हो और आर्थिक विवशता के कारण उन्हें अपनी आयु या शक्ति के प्रतिकूल कार्यों में न जाना पड़े।
4. कथन IV सही है (अनुच्छेद 45): 86वें संविधान संशोधन, 2002 द्वारा संशोधित किया गया। यह निर्देश देता है कि राज्य छह वर्ष की आयु पूरी करने तक सभी बालकों के लिए 'प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखरेख और शिक्षा' (ECCE) की व्यवस्था करने का प्रयास करेगा।

(इसके अतिरिक्त, अनुच्छेद 39(f) बच्चों के गरिमामय विकास की गारंटी देता है और अनुच्छेद 51A(k) माता-पिता पर 6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को शिक्षा का अवसर देने का मूल कर्तव्य आरोपित करता है)।

अतः I, II, III और IV सभी सही हैं, इसलिए विकल्प (D) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II, III and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Indian Constitution provides comprehensive child rights safeguards: Article 21A guarantees free, compulsory education for children aged 6–14; Article 24 prohibits hazardous child labor; Article 39(e) protects children’s tender age from abuse; and Article 45 directs early childhood care and education below age six, demonstrating complete constitutional coverage across all provisions.

questions.question_hindi: एक प्रधानाचार्य एक शिक्षक द्वारा प्रस्तुत सामाजिक विज्ञान पाठ योजना की समीक्षा कर रहे हैं। पाठ का विषय 'स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार' है। पाठ योजना पूरी तरह से छात्रों द्वारा श्यामपट्ट से अनुच्छेद 19 के कानूनी पाठ को अपनी कॉपियों में नकल करने पर आधारित है। मानवाधिकार शिक्षा को बढ़ावा देने वाले एक शैक्षिक नेता के रूप में, प्रधानाचार्य को क्या प्रतिपुष्टि (feedback) देनी चाहिए?
options_hindi: पाठ योजना को स्वीकृत करना, क्योंकि संवैधानिक कानूनी पाठ का सटीक रटन मानवाधिकार शिक्षा का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य है।
व्यावहारिक अनुप्रयोग को बढ़ावा देने के लिए वाक् एवं अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता पर केस स्टडीज (केस अध्ययनों) का उपयोग करने का सुझाव देना ('मानवाधिकारों के लिए शिक्षा')।
शिक्षक को निर्देश देना कि वह इस विषय को पाठ्यक्रम से पूरी तरह हटा दे क्योंकि वाक् स्वतंत्रता विद्यालय के लिए अत्यधिक विवादास्पद है।
शिक्षक को सलाह देना कि औपचारिक लिखावट कौशल का अभ्यास कराने के लिए छात्रों के लेखन कार्य को काफी लंबा कर दे।

questions.question_english: A Principal is reviewing a social science lesson plan submitted by a faculty member on the topic 'The Right to Freedom'. The submitted plan relies entirely on students copying the verbatim legal text of Article 19 from the blackboard into their notebooks. As an educational leader fostering Human Rights Education, what professional guidance should the Principal provide?
options_english: Approve the instructional plan as submitted, since verbatim memorization of constitutional text represents the primary objective of HRE.
Advise integrating interactive case studies on freedom of speech to foster critical application ('Education for human rights').
Direct the teacher to excise the topic entirely from the instructional syllabus because civil liberties are excessively contentious for school-aged pupils.
Instruct the teacher to substantially expand the volume of mechanical copying in order to drill formal cursive handwriting skills.
questions.explanation_english: The three recognized pedagogical pillars of Human Rights Education (HRE) are: 'Education about human rights' (learning factual norms and laws), 'Education through human rights' (experiencing rights in pedagogical interactions), and 'Education for human rights' (empowering learners to apply rights in real life to protect themselves and others). Having students merely copy the constitutional text of Article 19 (Right to Freedom) from the chalkboard into their notebooks reduces human rights to passive, rote memorization without contextual understanding. A visionary school principal and educational leader should guide the teacher to incorporate participatory case studies exploring freedom of speech, press freedom, and reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2). This pedagogical approach facilitates 'Education for human rights,' enabling students to understand how constitutional protections operate in real-world scenarios, how rights intersect with democratic responsibilities, and how citizens navigate institutional challenges.
questions.explanation_hindi: मानवाधिकार शिक्षा (HRE) के तीन प्रमुख स्तंभ हैं: 'मानवाधिकारों के बारे में शिक्षा', 'मानवाधिकारों के माध्यम से शिक्षा' और 'मानवाधिकारों के लिए शिक्षा' (Education for human rights)। छात्रों द्वारा श्यामपट्ट (board) से अनुच्छेद 19 (स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार) के कानूनी पाठ को केवल अपनी कॉपियों में नकल कर लेना रटंत प्रणाली को बढ़ावा देता है, जिससे अधिकार की वास्तविक समझ विकसित नहीं होती। एक कुशल संस्था प्रमुख और शैक्षिक प्रशासक के रूप में, प्रधानाचार्य को शिक्षक को यह सलाह देनी चाहिए कि वे भाषण और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता तथा उस पर अनुच्छेद 19(2) के तहत लागू युक्तियुक्त निबंधनों से संबंधित वास्तविक केस अध्ययनों (case studies) का उपयोग करें। यह पद्धति 'मानवाधिकारों के लिए शिक्षा' को बढ़ावा देती है, जिससे विद्यार्थी अधिकारों के व्यावहारिक अनुप्रयोग, लोकतांत्रिक दायित्वों और संवैधानिक उपचारों को गहराई से समझ पाते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Suggest using case studies on freedom of speech to foster application (Education for human rights).

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Human Rights Education aims to translate legal provisions into practical real-world application (“Education for human rights”). Rather than relying on passive board-copying or rote memorization of constitutional text, effective pedagogy utilizes interactive case studies on freedom of speech, encouraging students to analyze rights claims, evaluate societal responsibilities, and apply concepts critically.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): National sovereignty cannot be invoked by a State as an impenetrable shield to preclude international scrutiny of gross domestic human rights violations.
Reason (R): Contemporary international human rights jurisprudence recognizes that the promotion and protection of fundamental human rights constitutes a legitimate and erga omnes concern of the international community.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) provides the direct and correct conceptual explanation of (A):
- Historical Context & Evolution: Under classical international law (the 1648 Treaty of Westphalia and Article 2(7) of the UN Charter), the principle of national sovereignty and non-intervention held that how a sovereign government treated its own nationals fell exclusively within its domestic jurisdiction.
- The Post-WWII Paradigm Shift: The horrors of the Holocaust and the adoption of the UN Charter (Articles 55 and 56), the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), the Genocide Convention (1948), and the Geneva Conventions fundamentally altered this doctrine. Human rights obligations are now recognized as 'erga omnes' obligations—legal duties owed to the international community as a whole.
- The Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action (1993) explicitly settled this question by affirming that the promotion and protection of all human rights is a 'legitimate concern of the international community' and does not violate state sovereignty.
- Consequently, when gross, systematic violations of human rights occur, sovereign nations can no longer invoke domestic jurisdiction to shield themselves from international scrutiny, reporting procedures by UN Special Rapporteurs, investigations by the UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC), or universal jurisdiction under the International Criminal Court (ICC).
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही और सटीक स्पष्टीकरण प्रस्तुत करता है:
- ऐतिहासिक पृष्ठभूमि: पारंपरिक वेस्टफेलियाई संप्रभुता व्यवस्था तथा संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर के अनुच्छेद 2(7) के अंतर्गत यह माना जाता था कि राज्य के आंतरिक मामले संप्रभुता के दायरे में आते हैं और कोई भी बाहरी शक्ति किसी देश द्वारा अपने नागरिकों के साथ किए जाने वाले व्यवहार में हस्तक्षेप नहीं कर सकती।
- आधुनिक न्यायशास्त्रीय परिवर्तन: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के नरसंहारों के बाद संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर (अनुच्छेद 55 व 56), UDHR (1948) तथा 1993 के वियना घोषणापत्र ने यह अकाट्य सिद्धांत स्थापित किया कि मानवाधिकारों की रक्षा संपूर्ण अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुदाय का 'वैध सरोकार' (Legitimate Concern) है तथा यह 'एर्गा ओम्नेस' (Erga Omnes - समस्त विश्व के प्रति बाध्यकारी) दायित्व है।
- अतः यदि कोई राज्य अपनी सीमाओं के भीतर व्यापक स्तर पर मानवाधिकारों का हनन, जातीय नरसंहार या युद्ध अपराध करता है, तो वह संप्रभुता का बहाना बनाकर संयुक्त राष्ट्र मानवाधिकार परिषद (UNHRC), अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आपराधिक न्यायालय (ICC) या वैश्विक संवीक्षा व प्रतिबंधों से खुद का बचाव नहीं कर सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Modern international law establishes that human rights protections transcend domestic boundaries and state sovereignty, making severe rights violations legitimate international concerns. Consequently, sovereign states cannot invoke non-interference in internal affairs to shield themselves from international scrutiny, diplomatic sanctions, or judicial investigations when committing widespread human rights abuses or systematically failing to protect their citizens.

questions.question_english: Which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) serves as the foundational cornerstone for personal liberty by guaranteeing that "Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person"?
options_english: Article 1
Article 3
Article 5
Article 9
questions.explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) Article 3.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text and Scope of Article 3: Article 3 of the UDHR succinctly proclaims: 'Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person.' It constitutes the bedrock of civil liberties, forming the gateway right without which no other economic, social, or political right can be exercised.
2. Inherent Triad of Rights:
   - Right to Life: Absolute protection against arbitrary deprivation of life.
   - Right to Liberty: Freedom from unlawful custody, physical restraint, and arbitrary imprisonment.
   - Security of Person: Protection against physical assault, bodily injury, and harassment by state or private actors.
3. Comparison with Indian Constitution: Article 3 of the UDHR directly corresponds to Article 21 of the Constitution of India ('Protection of life and personal liberty: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law'). The Supreme Court of India in landmark decisions (e.g., Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978, and K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017) has interpreted Article 21 in light of Article 3 of the UDHR.
4. Other Articles in Options:
   - Article 1: Equality in dignity and rights, reason and conscience.
   - Article 5: Prohibition of torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment.
   - Article 9: Prohibition of arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) अनुच्छेद 3।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. अनुच्छेद 3 का मूल पाठ एवं क्षेत्र: UDHR का अनुच्छेद 3 घोषणा करता है कि 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को जीवन, स्वतंत्रता और वैयक्तिक सुरक्षा का अधिकार है' (Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person)। यह सभी नागरिक स्वतंत्रताओं का मूल आधार है।
2. तीन मूलभूत घटक:
   (i) जीवन का अधिकार: मनमाने ढंग से जीवन से वंचित किए जाने से सुरक्षा।

questions.question_english: Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) articulates the philosophical foundation of all fundamental human rights. Which two essential moral/rational faculties does it explicitly affirm that all human beings are endowed with?
options_english: Liberty and Property
Reason and Conscience
Equality and Fraternity

questions.explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) Reason and Conscience.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text of Article 1 of the UDHR: 'All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.'
2. Jurisprudential Significance: Article 1 establishes the universal moral ontology of human rights based on natural law and Enlightenment philosophy:
   a. Reason (बुद्धि/तर्कशक्ति): Denotes human capacity for rational thought, intellectual deliberation, moral judgment, and understanding of right and wrong.
   b. Conscience (अंतरात्मा/विवेक): Denotes the innate moral compass, internal ethical awareness, and capacity for empathy toward fellow humans.
3. Constitutional Reflection in India: This philosophical premise directly aligns with the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, which resolves to secure 'Dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation', and Article 51A(e) which enjoins every citizen to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) बुद्धि और अंतरात्मा/विवेक (Reason and Conscience)।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR के अनुच्छेद 1 का मूल पाठ: 'सभी मानव जन्म से स्वतंत्र तथा गरिमा और अधिकारों के मामले में समान हैं। उन्हें बुद्धि और अंतरात्मा (Reason and Conscience) की देन प्राप्त है और उन्हें परस्पर भाईचारे की भावना के साथ व्यवहार करना चाहिए।'
2. दार्शनिक एवं नैतिक आधार: यह अनुच्छेद प्राकृतिक विधि (Natural Law) और कांटवादी गरिमा (Kantian Dignity) के सिद्धांत पर आधारित है। यह स्पष्ट करता है कि प्रत्येक व्यक्ति में तर्कसंगत सोच ('बुद्धि') और नैतिक निर्णय लेने की आंतरिक क्षमता ('अंतरात्मा' या 'विवेक') जन्मजात होती है, जो मनुष्य को अन्य जीवों से अलग करती है और सार्वभौमिक मानवीय गरिमा का आधार बनती है।
3. भारतीय संविधान में समानांतर प्रावधान: भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में वर्णित 'बंधुता' (Fraternity) और 'व्यक्ति की गरिमा' (Dignity of the Individual) तथा अनुच्छेद 51क(ङ) में उल्लिखित 'समान भ्रातृत्व की भावना' अनुच्छेद 1 के इसी दर्शन को परिलक्षित करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Reason and Conscience

It explicitly highlights that every individual is endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of shared human brotherhood.

questions.question_english: Corporal punishment in schools is explicitly recognized as a human rights violation because it directly infringes upon which fundamental rights?
options_english: Right to freedom of speech, personal expression, and academic opinion in school
Right to dignity, bodily integrity, and protection from cruel treatment
Fundamental constitutional right to freedom of religion and personal conscience
Universal right to freedom of peaceful assembly and student association
questions.explanation_english:
Corporal punishment in educational institutions violates core human rights principles:
1. **Inviolable Human Dignity and Bodily Integrity:** Under **Article 21 of the Constitution of India** (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) and **Article 37(a) of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**, every child has the right to physical integrity, human dignity, and protection from torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
2. **UNCRC General Comment No. 8 (2006):** Explicitly defines corporal punishment as any punishment in which physical force is used and intended to cause some degree of pain or discomfort, however light, and declares it incompatible with the dignity of the child.
3. **Judicial Precedent:** In *Parents Forum for Meaningful Education v. Union of India (2001)*, the Delhi High Court struck down provisions allowing corporal punishment, holding that inflicting physical pain on a child violates fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 21.
4. **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR):** Issued comprehensive Guidelines for Eliminating Corporal Punishment in Schools, reinforcing zero-tolerance across all educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में शारीरिक दंड (Corporal Punishment) बुनियादी मानवाधिकारों का घोर उल्लंघन है:
1. **शारीरिक अखंडता और मानवीय गरिमा:** **भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21** (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार) तथा **बाल अधिकारों पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र अभिसमय (UNCRC) के अनुच्छेद 37(a) व 19** के अनुसार प्रत्येक बच्चे को शारीरिक अखंडता, व्यक्तिगत गरिमा और किसी भी क्रूर, अमानवीय या अपमानजनक व्यवहार से पूर्ण संरक्षण का अधिकार प्राप्त है।
2. **UNCRC की सामान्य टिप्पणी संख्या 8 (2006):** स्पष्ट करती है कि शारीरिक दंड चाहे कितना भी हल्का क्यों न हो, वह बच्चे की अंतर्निहित गरिमा और अधिकारों के सर्वथा विपरीत है।
3. **न्यायिक निर्णय:** दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय ने *पैरेंट्स फोरम फॉर मीनिंगफुल एजुकेशन बनाम भारत संघ (2001)* मामले में शारीरिक दंड की अनुमति देने वाले नियमों को असंवैधानिक घोषित करते हुए इसे संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 (समानता) और 21 (गरिमापूर्ण जीवन) का सीधा उल्लंघन ठहराया था।
4. **NCPCR दिशानिर्देश:** राष्ट्रीय बाल अधिकार संरक्षण आयोग (NCPCR) ने स्कूलों में शारीरिक दंड के उन्मूलन के लिए विस्तृत नियम बनाए हैं, जिसके तहत किसी भी प्रकार का शारीरिक या मानसिक प्रताड़न पूर्णतः वर्जित है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 36(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what is the legal position of a State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) if a specific human rights violation is already being inquired into by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) or another statutory Commission?
options_english: The SHRC must conduct a parallel inquiry and submit a joint investigation report with the NHRC.
The SHRC shall act as the appellate authority over the NHRC's findings.
The SHRC shall not inquire into the matter.
The SHRC can take over the inquiry if the State Government demands it.
questions.explanation_english:
Section 36(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 explicitly prevents duplicate or parallel proceedings between statutory oversight bodies.
Statutory Principles:
1. Statutory Bar on Parallel Inquiries: Section 36(1) provides: "The Commission shall not inquire into any matter which is pending before a State Commission or any other Commission duly constituted under any law for the time being in force."
2. Reciprocal Bar on SHRC: Similarly, the proviso to Section 21(5) provides that if any matter is being inquired into by the NHRC or any other statutory commission, the State Commission shall not inquire into the said matter.
3. Judicial Harmony: This prevents jurisdictional conflict, double jeopardy, and contradictory findings between concurrent statutory tribunals. Once the NHRC takes cognizance of an incident, the SHRC is statutorily ousted from inquiring into that same matter.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 36(1) और धारा 21(5) का परंतुक स्पष्ट रूप से मुकदमों के दोहरेपन और क्षेत्राधिकार के टकराव को रोकने का नियम निर्धारित करते हैं।
वैधानिक सिद्धांत:
1. समानांतर कार्यवाही पर रोक: धारा 36(1) यह स्पष्ट करती है कि राष्ट्रीय आयोग ऐसे किसी मामले की जांच नहीं करेगा जो किसी राज्य आयोग या किसी अन्य विधिमान्य सांविधिक आयोग के समक्ष पहले से लंबित हो।
2. एसएचआरसी पर समान प्रतिबंध: धारा 21(5) के परंतुक के अनुसार यदि राष्ट्रीय आयोग (NHRC) किसी मामले की जांच कर रहा है, तो राज्य आयोग उस मामले में समानांतर जांच नहीं कर सकता।
3. न्यायिक समन्वय: इसका उद्देश्य प्रशासनिक भ्रम, परस्पर विरोधी निर्णयों तथा एक ही मामले में दोहरे क्षेत्राधिकार को समाप्त करना है। अतः एनएचआरसी द्वारा संज्ञान लिए जाने पर एसएचआरसी उस मामले की जांच नहीं कर सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The SHRC shall not inquire into the matter.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 36(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act prevents duplicate proceedings between oversight bodies. If the National Human Rights Commission or any other statutory commission is already inquiring into a human rights violation, the State Human Rights Commission is statutorily barred from initiating or continuing a parallel inquiry into the same matter.

questions.question_english: Article 2 of the UNCRC guarantees the principle of "Non-discrimination". It obligates States Parties to respect and ensure all convention rights to each child within their jurisdiction without discrimination of any kind, irrespective of the characteristics or status of which persons?
options_english: Exclusively the individual child, without reference to family members
Only children possessing formal citizenship and legal documentation
The child, or his or her parents, or legal guardians
Only personal attributes over which the minor exercises direct individual control
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (C). Article 2 of the UNCRC establishes an expansive, comprehensive shield against discrimination, explicitly extending protection based not only on the child's own characteristics, but also on those of their parents or legal guardians.

Key Legal Aspects of Article 2:
1. Article 2(1) Text: "States Parties shall respect and ensure the rights set forth in the present Convention to each child within their jurisdiction without discrimination of any kind, irrespective of the child's or his or her parent's or legal guardian's race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national, ethnic or social origin, property, disability, birth or other status."
2. Protection Against Vicarious Punishment (Article 2(2)): States Parties are obligated to take all appropriate measures to ensure that the child is protected against all forms of discrimination or punishment on the basis of the status, activities, expressed opinions, or beliefs of the child's parents, legal guardians, or family members.
3. Constitutional Congruence: In India, this aligns with Article 14 (Equality before Law) and Article 15 (Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth). Under Section 8 and Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, 2009, schools cannot deny admission or discriminate against children based on the economic, social, or marital status of their parents.
questions.explanation_hindi:

अनुच्छेद 2 के प्रमुख विधिक तत्व:
1. अनुच्छेद 2(1) का प्रावधान: राज्य पक्षकार अपने क्षेत्राधिकार के भीतर प्रत्येक बालक को कन्वेंशन के सभी अधिकार बिना किसी भेदभाव के सुनिश्चित करेंगे, चाहे बालक अथवा उसके माता-पिता अथवा विधिक अभिभावक की जाति, रंग, लिंग, भाषा, धर्म, राजनीतिक या अन्य विचार, राष्ट्रीय, नृजातीय या सामाजिक मूल, संपत्ति, दिव्यांगता, जन्म अथवा अन्य कोई प्रस्थिति कैसी भी क्यों न हो।
2. पारिवारिक पृष्ठभूमि के आधार पर दंड से संरक्षण (अनुच्छेद 2(2)): राज्य यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि माता-पिता या अभिभावकों की गतिविधियों, विचारों या सामाजिक स्थिति के आधार पर बच्चे के साथ कोई भेदभाव न हो और न ही उसे कोई दंड भुगतना पड़े।
3. भारतीय संविधान और विधियों से सामंजस्य: यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 और अनुच्छेद 15 के अनुरूप है। शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम (RTE Act), 2009 की धारा 8 और 12(1)(c) भी स्पष्ट करती है कि किसी बच्चे को उसके माता-पिता की आर्थिक, सामाजिक या वैवाहिक स्थिति के आधार पर दाखिले से वंचित या प्रताड़ित नहीं किया जा सकता।

questions.question_english: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what is the statutory period of limitation barring the National Human Rights Commission from inquiring into a human rights violation?
options_english: The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of six months from the date of the incident
The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the violation is alleged to have been committed
The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of three years from the date of the incident
There is no period of limitation; human rights violations can be inquired into at any time
questions.explanation_english:
Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 lays down a strict bar on the jurisdiction of the Commission with respect to older complaints: 'The Commission or the State Commission shall not inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.'
This one-year limitation period is designed to prevent stale claims, ensure prompt reporting and swift investigation while evidence remains fresh and witnesses are accessible. However, if a violation is of a continuing nature (continuing wrong), the limitation clock may run from the last date of such continued violation as interpreted by judicial precedents.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 36(2) के अंतर्गत आयोग के अधिकार क्षेत्र पर एक स्पष्ट वैधानिक समय-सीमा (Limitation Period) लगाई गई है। इस उपधारा के अनुसार: 'आयोग या राज्य आयोग ऐसे किसी मामले की जाँच नहीं करेगा जो उस तारीख से एक वर्ष (one year) की समाप्ति के बाद प्रस्तुत किया गया हो जिस तारीख को मानव अधिकारों के उल्लंघन का कथित कृत्य किया गया था।'
इस प्रावधान का उद्देश्य शिकायतों की शीघ्र रिपोर्टिंग को प्रोत्साहित करना, बासी मामलों (stale claims) से बचना तथा साक्ष्यों और गवाहों की प्रामाणिकता बनी रहने के दौरान त्वरित जाँच सुनिश्चित करना है। अतः घटना की तिथि से 1 वर्ष बीत जाने के बाद NHRC मामले की जाँच नहीं कर सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 imposes a strict statutory limitation period on the Commission’s jurisdiction. The National Human Rights Commission is legally barred from inquiring into any human rights violation complaint if it is submitted after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged incident.

questions.question_english: Which district-level quasi-judicial statutory body is empowered under Chapter V of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 with powers equivalent to a Judicial Magistrate First Class to make binding decisions regarding the care, protection, and rehabilitation of a 'Child in Need of Care and Protection'?
options_english: The District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
The Child Welfare Committee (CWC)
The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB)
The District Human Rights Court
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 27 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the State Government is statutorily mandated to constitute for every district one or more Child Welfare Committees (CWC). The Committee consists of a Chairperson and four other members, of whom at least one must be a woman and another an expert on matters concerning children. Under Section 27(9) and Section 29, the Committee functions as a quasi-judicial bench and is vested with the powers conferred by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 on a Judicial Magistrate of First Class. It has exclusive jurisdiction to deal with all proceedings relating to children in need of care and protection, ordering institutional care, sponsorship, foster care, or legal adoption.
questions.explanation_hindi: किशोर न्याय (बालकों की देखरेख और संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2015 की धारा 27 के तहत प्रत्येक जिले में राज्य सरकार द्वारा एक या अधिक 'बाल कल्याण समिति' (CWC) का गठन अनिवार्य है। इस समिति में एक अध्यक्ष और चार अन्य सदस्य होते हैं, जिनमें कम से कम एक महिला और एक बाल मामलों का विशेषज्ञ होना अनिवार्य है। धारा 27(9) और धारा 29 के तहत CWC एक अर्ध-न्यायिक पीठ के रूप में कार्य करती है और इसे दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता (CrPC) के तहत प्रथम श्रेणी न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट (JMFC) की शक्तियां प्राप्त हैं। जिले में देखरेख और संरक्षण के जरूरतमंद किसी भी बच्चे की सुरक्षा, अभिरक्षा, संस्थागत देखरेख, पालक देखरेख और सामाजिक पुनर्वास के अंतिम आदेश देने का वैधानिक क्षेत्राधिकार CWC के पास है।

Vested with powers equivalent to a magistrate court, the CWC makes binding decisions regarding the care, custody, protection, rehabilitation, and social reintegration of children in need.

questions.question_english: Under Article 3(1) of the UNCRC, in all actions concerning children, whether undertaken by public or private social welfare institutions, courts of law, administrative authorities, or legislative bodies, what must be a primary consideration?
options_english: The budgetary resources and financial constraints of the State
The best interests of the child
The preservation and supremacy of parental authority
The cultural and customary traditions of the local community
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (B). Article 3(1) of the UNCRC states: "In all actions concerning children, whether undertaken by public or private social welfare institutions, courts of law, administrative authorities or legislative bodies, the best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration."

Significance of the Principle:
1. Tripartite Legal Concept: The UN Committee on the Rights of the Child in General Comment No. 14 (2013) explained that the 'best interests' concept is threefold: (a) a substantive right, (b) a fundamental, interpretive legal principle, and (c) a rule of procedure requiring impact assessment on the child in every decision.
2. Non-Derogable Baseline: While it is described as "a primary consideration" (acknowledging potential balancing with competing public interests), it carries profound legal weight, requiring institutions to demonstrate that the child's welfare and rights were prioritized.
3. Indian Law: The principle is codified into Indian statutes, notably Section 3(iv) of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 ("Principle of best interest: All decisions regarding the child shall be based on the primary consideration that they are in the best interest of the child"), POCSO Act 2012, and custody/guardianship jurisprudence under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (B) है। UNCRC के अनुच्छेद 3(1) में स्पष्ट प्रावधान है: "बच्चों से संबंधित सभी कार्यों में, चाहे वे सार्वजनिक या निजी समाज कल्याण संस्थाओं, न्यायालयों, प्रशासनिक अधिकारियों या विधायी निकायों द्वारा किए जाएं, बालक का सर्वोत्तम हित (Best interests of the child) एक प्राथमिक विचार होगा।"

सिद्धांत का विधिक महत्व:
1. त्रिपक्षीय विधिक अवधारणा: बाल अधिकार समिति ने सामान्य टिप्पणी संख्या 14 (2013) में स्पष्ट किया है कि सर्वोत्तम हित: (क) एक मौलिक अधिकार है, (ख) एक व्याख्यात्मक विधिक सिद्धांत है, और (ग) एक प्रक्रियात्मक नियम है जिसके तहत निर्णय लेते समय बच्चे पर पड़ने वाले प्रभावों का अनिवार्य मूल्यांकन आवश्यक है।
2. प्राथमिकता: यद्यपि इसे 'एक प्राथमिक विचार' कहा गया है, लेकिन यह किसी भी अन्य प्रशासनिक या वित्तीय सुविधा की तुलना में अत्यधिक विधिक भार रखता है।
3. भारतीय कानूनों में समावेशन: यह सिद्धांत भारतीय कानूनों में मजबूती से अंतर्निहित है, जैसे किशोर न्याय अधिनियम, 2015 की धारा 3(iv) ('सर्वोत्तम हित का सिद्धांत'), पॉक्सो अधिनियम 2012, तथा संरक्षक और प्रतिपाल्य अधिनियम, 1890 के तहत अभिरक्षा (Custody) से संबंधित अदालती निर्णयों में।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The best interests of the child

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 3(1) of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child establishes the overarching legal mandate that in all actions concerning children—whether undertaken by public or private social welfare institutions, courts, administrative authorities, or legislative bodies— the best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration guiding all decisions.

questions.question_english: For conducting cases in a Human Rights Court under Section 31 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what is the minimum professional experience required for an advocate to be appointed as a Special Public Prosecutor by the State Government?
options_english: Practice as an advocate for not less than five years
Practice as an advocate for not less than seven years
Practice as an advocate for not less than ten years
Practice as an advocate for not less than fifteen years
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 31 of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the State Government is statutorily required to specify a Public Prosecutor or appoint an advocate who has been in practice as an advocate for not less than seven years as a Special Public Prosecutor for conducting cases in a Human Rights Court.
Key Legal Details:
1. Statutory Provision: Section 31 states: "For every Human Rights Court, the State Government shall, by notification, specify a Public Prosecutor or appoint an advocate who has been in practice as an advocate for not less than seven years, as a Special Public Prosecutor for the purpose of conducting cases in that Court."
2. Alignment with Criminal Procedure: The 7-year experience requirement mirrors the general benchmark set under Section 24(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) and Section 18(7) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for Special Public Prosecutors.
3. Distinct from 10-Year Limits: While some specialized laws (like the NDPS Act or POCSO in certain states) require 10 years for special public prosecutors, Section 31 of the PHRA specifically sets the minimum bar at 7 years.

मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 31 के अनुसार, मानवाधिकार न्यायालय में मामलों के संचालन के लिए राज्य सरकार द्वारा विशेष लोक अभियोजक के रूप में नियुक्त किए जाने वाले अधिवक्ता के पास कम से कम 7 वर्ष की वकालत का अनुभव होना अनिवार्य है।

1. धारा 31 का पाठ: "प्रत्येक मानवाधिकार न्यायालय के लिए, राज्य सरकार अधिसूचना द्वारा किसी लोक अभियोजक को विनिर्दिष्ट करेगी या किसी ऐसे अधिवक्ता को, जो कम से कम सात वर्ष से अधिवक्ता के रूप में व्यवसाय कर रहा हो, विशेष लोक अभियोजक नियुक्त करेगी।"
2. आपराधिक न्याय संहिता से सामंजस्य: यह 7 वर्ष की अर्हता दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता (CrPC) की धारा 24(8) तथा भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता, 2023 (BNSS) की धारा 18(7) के तहत विहित अर्हता के अनुरूप है।
3. 10 वर्ष से भिन्नता: अन्य कुछ विशेष अधिनियमों में 10 वर्ष का अनुभव मांगा जाता है, किंतु मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम की धारा 31 में यह सीमा स्पष्ट रूप से 'न्यूनतम 7 वर्ष' निर्धारित है।

questions.question_english: In the legal framework of child rights and juvenile jurisprudence in India, what role does the doctrine of 'parens patriae' assign to the State?
options_english: The State acts as the ultimate parent and sovereign protector of children who cannot protect themselves
The State must defer all decisions regarding children strictly to their biological parents
The State is entitled to treat children as economic property for national goals
The State enjoys absolute immunity from liability for any harm suffered by children in state care
questions.explanation_english:
The doctrine of 'parens patriae' (Latin for 'parent of the nation') establishes the inherent sovereign duty of the State to act as supreme guardian and protector of persons suffering legal disability, particularly children, who cannot protect their own rights and interests.

Key Principles:
1. Sovereign Protective Power: Originating in English equity jurisprudence, the doctrine recognizes that the sovereign has an overarching obligation to safeguard minors, orphaned, abandoned, or abused children who lack capable guardianship.
2. Application in Indian Jurisprudence: The Supreme Court of India has invoked this doctrine in landmark cases (e.g., Charan Lal Sahu v. Union of India, Gaurav Jain v. Union of India, and various child custody and adoption decisions), ruling that where natural guardians fail to protect a child's best interests, the State must step in in loco parentis.
3. Statutory Manifestation: The doctrine underpins India's Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, authorizing Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) and statutory child protection authorities to intervene, provide institutional care, and protect children in need of care and protection (CNCP).

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
'पेरेंस पैट्रिए' (Parens Patriae) का सिद्धांत:

1. शाब्दिक अर्थ एवं उत्पत्ति: लैटिन भाषा के इस शब्द का अर्थ 'राष्ट्र का पिता' या 'सर्वोच्च अभिभावक' (parent of the nation) होता है। यह आंग्ल सामान्य विधि (Common Law) से उत्पन्न हुआ सिद्धांत है, जिसके अनुसार राज्य उन व्यक्तियों का अंतिम संप्रभु संरक्षक होता है जो अपनी अल्पायु, अक्षमता या लाचारी के कारण स्वयं अपने हितों की रक्षा नहीं कर सकते।
2. भारतीय न्यायशास्त्र में भूमिका: भारतीय सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने अनेक ऐतिहासिक मामलों (जैसे गौरव जैन बनाम भारत संघ, चरण लाल साहू बनाम भारत संघ) में इस सिद्धांत को लागू किया है। इसके अनुसार यदि माता-पिता या प्राकृतिक संरक्षक किसी बच्चे की उपेक्षा करते हैं, उसका शोषण करते हैं अथवा बच्चा अनाथ हो जाता है, तो राज्य का यह वैधानिक और संवैधानिक कर्तव्य है कि वह आगे आकर बच्चे के सर्वोत्तम हित में उसके संरक्षक की भूमिका निभाए।
3. विधिक प्रकटीकरण: किशोर न्याय (बालकों की देखरेख और संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2015 (JJ Act) और बाल कल्याण समितियों (CWC) की संपूर्ण कार्यप्रणाली इसी सिद्धांत पर आधारित है, जो देखरेख और संरक्षण के जरूरतमंद बच्चों को आश्रय, पोषण और विधिक सुरक्षा प्रदान करती है।

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The State is the ultimate parent and protector of children who cannot protect themselves.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The doctrine of ‘parens patriae’ translates to “parent of the nation” and establishes the legal duty of the State to act as the ultimate sovereign protector of vulnerable individuals. Applied to child rights, it empowers state authorities to intervene and safeguard children who suffer neglect, abuse, or lack adequate parental care and guardianship.

questions.question_english: A non-governmental organization (NGO) specializing in child rights uncovers an organized child trafficking ring operating near government schools. The NGO wishes to engage the statutory framework under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 to push for systemic institutional safeguards. Under which specific provision of the Act is the NHRC mandated to encourage and collaborate with NGOs?
options_english: Section 12(i), mandating the Commission to encourage the efforts of non-governmental organizations working in human rights
Section 18, which empowers recognized NGOs to issue legally binding administrative directions to schools
Section 14, which grants certified NGOs formal investigative police powers
Section 36, which explicitly prohibits the NHRC from officially collaborating with non-state NGOs
questions.explanation_english:
Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 enumerates the statutory functions of the National Human Rights Commission. Under clause (i) of Section 12, the Act explicitly lays down that the Commission shall:
"encourage the efforts of non-governmental organisations and institutions working in the field of human rights."

Significance of Section 12(i):
1. Legislative Recognition: Recognizing that statutory oversight bodies cannot independently detect every grassroots human rights violation, Parliament specifically mandated formal collaboration with civil society organizations.
2. NGO Core Group: The NHRC operationalizes Section 12(i) by maintaining a specialized NGO Core Group that meets regularly to consult on pressing issues like child labor, child trafficking, custodial violence, and rights of disabled persons.
3. Analysis of Incorrect Options:
   - Section 18 outlines inquiry steps (recommending compensation, prosecution, or interim relief); it does not grant NGOs power to issue binding administrative orders.
   - Section 14 allows the Commission to utilize governmental investigation agencies with governmental concurrence, not private NGOs.
   - Section 36 outlines jurisdictional limitation periods and bar on matters pending before other commissions.

Thus, Option (A) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 12 में राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग के कृत्यों (Functions) का विस्तृत विवरण दिया गया है।

2. एनजीओ कोर ग्रुप: NHRC ने धारा 12(i) को प्रभावी बनाने के लिए एक 'एनजीओ कोर ग्रुप' का गठन किया है, जो आयोग के साथ नियमित बैठकें कर नीतिगत सुधारों पर विमर्श करता है।

   - धारा 36 आयोग के अधिकार क्षेत्र की सीमाओं से संबंधित है।

questions.question_english: What is the eligibility criterion for appointment as the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) following the amendments introduced by the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019?
options_english: A person who has been a Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court
Exclusively and strictly a person who has served as the Chief Justice of a High Court
A judicial officer who has served as a District and Sessions Judge for a minimum of ten years
An eminent retired bureaucrat who has served at the rank of Chief Secretary to the State Government
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 21(2)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, as amended by the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) must be a person who has been a Chief Justice OR a Judge of a High Court.
Evolution and Statutory Impact:
1. Prior to 2019: Section 21(2)(a) stipulated that only a former Chief Justice of a High Court could head an SHRC. Due to the limited availability of retired High Court Chief Justices in individual states, numerous SHRCs remained headless for months or years.
2. 2019 Broadening: To alleviate institutional bottlenecks and fill vacancies promptly, the 2019 Amendment expanded the qualification criteria to include former High Court Judges alongside Chief Justices.
3. Corresponding NHRC Change: Similarly, Section 3(2)(a) was amended in 2019 to permit former Supreme Court Judges (in addition to former Chief Justices of India) to be appointed as the Chairperson of the NHRC.

2019 संशोधन का प्रभाव:
1. 2019 से पूर्व की स्थिति: मूल 1993 के कानून में केवल उच्च न्यायालय के सेवानिवृत्त मुख्य न्यायाधीश ही अध्यक्ष बन सकते थे। इस प्रतिबंध के कारण कई राज्यों में वर्षों तक अध्यक्ष का पद रिक्त पड़ा रहता था।
2. 2019 में अहर्ता का विस्तार: रिक्तियों को शीघ्रता से भरने हेतु संसद ने 2019 में संशोधन कर उच्च न्यायालय के सेवानिवृत्त न्यायाधीशों को भी अध्यक्ष पद हेतु पात्र बना दिया।

questions.question_english: To ensure the speedy trial of offenses arising out of human rights violations, Section 30 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 provides for the establishment of specialized Human Rights Courts. At what level are these courts established?
options_english: At the State level (High Court)
At the District level
At the Sub-Divisional level
Only in metropolitan cities
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 30 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, Human Rights Courts are established at the District level.
Key Statutory Provisions:
1. District Level Designations: Section 30 provides that for providing speedy trial of offenses arising out of human rights violations, the State Government may, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, by notification, specify for each district a Court of Session to be a Human Rights Court.
2. Utilizing Existing Judiciary: Rather than setting up a parallel, expensive judicial cadre, the Act designates an existing Court of Session in each district to try human rights offenses.
3. Exception: Under the proviso to Section 30, if a Court of Session is already specified as a special court under any other existing law for such offenses (e.g., under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act), a separate designation is not required.

questions.question_english: Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 prescribes a special procedure regarding complaints alleging human rights violations by members of the Armed Forces. What is the statutory limitation imposed on the NHRC in such cases?
options_english: The NHRC is completely barred from taking cognizance and must dismiss the petition outright
The NHRC can conduct independent field investigations using its own investigation team
The NHRC may only call for a report from the Central Government and make recommendations based on that report
The NHRC can investigate armed forces personnel only upon a direct reference from the President of India
questions.explanation_english:
Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 sets forth a special and restrictive procedure dealing with human rights violations alleged to have been committed by members of the Armed Forces (defined under Section 2(1)(a) to include naval, military, and air forces, as well as any other armed forces of the Union).
Under Section 19(1):
(a) The Commission cannot deploy its own investigative team or summon armed forces personnel directly; it may, either on its own motion or on a petition, seek a report from the Central Government.
(b) After the receipt of the report, it may either not proceed with the complaint or, as the case may be, make its recommendations to that Government.
Under Section 19(2), the Central Government is required to inform the Commission of the action taken within three months (or extended time). Under Section 19(3), the Commission must publish its report along with its recommendations and the government's action. Hence, the Commission's power is limited to calling for a report from the Central Government and making recommendations.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 19 सशस्त्र बलों (थल सेना, नौसेना, वायु सेना और संघ के अन्य सशस्त्र बल) द्वारा किए गए कथित मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनों के मामलों में आयोग की शक्तियों को सीमित करती है। इस धारा के अंतर्गत:
1. NHRC स्वयं अपनी अन्वेषण विंग के माध्यम से सशस्त्र बलों के विरुद्ध प्रत्यक्ष स्वतंत्र जमीनी जाँच नहीं कर सकता।
2. धारा 19(1)(क) के तहत आयोग स्वप्रेरणा से या याचिका पर 'केंद्र सरकार से एक रिपोर्ट' (seek a report from the Central Government) मांग सकता है।
3. रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होने के बाद, धारा 19(1)(ख) के तहत आयोग मामले को समाप्त कर सकता है अथवा केंद्र सरकार को अपनी सिफारिशें (recommendations) भेज सकता है।
केंद्र सरकार को 3 माह के भीतर की गई कार्रवाई की जानकारी आयोग को देनी होती है, जिसे आयोग सार्वजनिक करता है। अतः आयोग की शक्ति केवल केंद्र सरकार से रिपोर्ट मांगने और उस पर अपनी सिफारिशें देने तक सीमित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) It may only seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act outlines a specialized procedure regarding alleged violations committed by members of the Armed Forces. The Commission cannot conduct independent direct investigations into military personnel; instead, it may seek a report from the Central Government and subsequently make non-binding recommendations or reports based on that information.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Under international human rights law, the obligation to provide free and compulsory primary education is subject to "progressive realization."
Reason (R): Developing nations lack the immediate resources to build schools and hire teachers simultaneously for all children.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
**Assertion (A) is False:**
Under international human rights law, particularly **Article 13(2)(a) and Article 14 of the ICESCR** as well as General Comment No. 11 (1999) and No. 13 (1999) of the CESCR, the provision of **free and compulsory primary education is an immediate core obligation**, NOT subject to progressive realization. States cannot plead lack of resources to avoid the immediate legal duty to ensure primary education without fees for all children. Progressive realization applies strictly to secondary, higher, and lifelong education.

**Reason (R) is True:**
As an empirical and socioeconomic reality, many developing nations face acute economic constraints and resource deficits, requiring phased infrastructure construction and gradual teacher recruitment drives.

Therefore, **Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true** (Option D).
questions.explanation_hindi:
**अभिकथन (A) गलत है:**
अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार कानून के तहत, विशेष रूप से **ICESCR के अनुच्छेद 13(2)(a) और 14** तथा संयुक्त राष्ट्र समिति (CESCR) की सामान्य टिप्पणी संख्या 11 एवं 13 के अनुसार, **निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य प्राथमिक शिक्षा प्रदान करना एक 'तात्कालिक एवं गैर-हस्तांतरणीय दायित्व' (Immediate Core Obligation) है**, न कि 'क्रमिक प्राप्ति' (Progressive Realization) का विषय। कोई भी देश आर्थिक संसाधनों की कमी का बहाना बनाकर बच्चों को मुफ्त प्राथमिक शिक्षा के विधिक अधिकार से वंचित नहीं कर सकता। 'क्रमिक प्राप्ति' का सिद्धांत केवल माध्यमिक और उच्च शिक्षा पर लागू होता है।

**कारण (R) सही है:**
विकासशील देशों में वित्तीय और संरचनात्मक संसाधनों की तात्कालिक कमी एक यथार्थपरक सामाजिक-आर्थिक वास्तविकता है, जिसके कारण स्कूलों के निर्माण और शिक्षकों के प्रशिक्षण में व्यावहारिक कठिनाइयों का सामना करना पड़ता है।

अतः **अभिकथन (A) असत्य है, परंतु कारण (R) सत्य है** (सही उत्तर D है)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under international human rights law, providing free and compulsory primary education is an immediate obligation rather than a subject of “progressive realization.” While economic resource constraints in developing nations explain practical infrastructure delays, the core legal mandate for primary education remains immediate, making the assertion false while the underlying reason accurately describes financial realities.

questions.question_english: Under the statutory framework of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, children who are victims of human rights violations—such as abandonment, child trafficking, severe abuse, or extreme exploitation—are classified under which legal category?
options_english: Child in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP)
Child in Conflict with Law (CCL)
Juvenile Offender undergoing Institutional Rehabilitation
Ward of the Court under Administrative Protective Custody
questions.explanation_english: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 makes a clear bifurcated distinction between two categories of children: (1) 'Child in Conflict with Law' (CCL) under Section 2(13), meaning a child who is alleged or found to have committed an offense; and (2) 'Child in Need of Care and Protection' (CNCP) under Section 2(14). Under Section 2(14), a CNCP includes any child found without home or settled place of abode, working in contravention of labour laws, residing with an unfit guardian, who has been abused, tortured, or exploited, who is vulnerable to trafficking or drug abuse, or who is mentally/physically disabled without caregiver support. CNCPs fall under the exclusive protective and rehabilitative jurisdiction of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC).
questions.explanation_hindi: किशोर न्याय (बालकों की देखरेख और संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2015 बच्चों को दो मुख्य कानूनी श्रेणियों में विभाजित करता है: (1) धारा 2(13) के तहत 'विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाला बालक' (Child in Conflict with Law - CCL), जिसने कोई अपराध किया हो या जिस पर आरोप हो (इनका मामला जुवेनाइल जस्टिस बोर्ड यानी JJB देखता है); तथा (2) धारा 2(14) के तहत 'देखरेख और संरक्षण का जरूरतमंद बालक' (Child in Need of Care and Protection - CNCP)। इसमें ऐसे बच्चे शामिल हैं जो बेघर, अनाथ, परित्यक्त, तस्करी के शिकार, बाल श्रम में लगे, शारीरिक/मानसिक यातना या गंभीर दुर्व्यवहार से पीड़ित हैं। ऐसे बच्चों के संरक्षण, पुनर्वास और आदेश जारी करने का विशेष अधिकार बाल कल्याण समिति (CWC) के पास होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Children in Need of Care and Protection

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 2(14) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, children facing extreme human rights violations, exploitation, trafficking, abandonment, or severe abuse are classified as “Children in Need of Care and Protection.” This legal categorization ensures statutory state intervention, protective custody, and comprehensive social rehabilitation.
